newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak refiner gains, SAX up 3.36 pts at 197.65.
newsitem.headline: Slovak refiner gains, SAX up 3.36 pts at 197.65.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Tuesday, with gains to crude oil refiner Slovnaft pushing the SAX index up 3.36 points to 197.65.
Slovnaft, the heaviest-weighted company in the index, gained 50 crowns, or 5.88 percent in continuous trading, to close at 900 crowns on relatively strong volume.
"The volume of 15,646 shares traded (in block trade) in Slovnaft is too large to afford for a domestic investor," Radovan Dzugas, a Creditanstalt broker, said.
The market has been watching the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) either to pullout or expand its 10.5 percent stake in Slovnaft.
The EBRD bought half the refiner's unsuccessful Global Depositary Receipts (GDR's) issue in 1995.
Brokers said they remain wary of the EBRD's position in Slovnaft despite a recent statment by the EBRD that it expected the Slovak National Property Fund (NPF) to buy back the stake.
"I rather see the NPF selling it's remaining 25 percent in Slovnaft due to probable illiquidity," Vladimir Kuklis, a CSOB Bank analyst, told Reuters.
Activity in Slovakia's largest investment fund, VUB Kupon, was strong on Tuesday with 15,494 shares traded, closing up five crowns at 745.
Overall volume slipped to 204,984 shares from 298,956 shares traded on Monday, as turnover fell to 160.34 million crowns from Monday's 217.19 million.
